Let $U={l,m,n,o}$ be the universal set and let $K={l,m,o}.$ What is $\overset{―}{K}?$
worked_solution:
The complement of $K,$ denoted $\overset{―}{K},$ consists of all the elements in $U$ that are not in $K.$ To represent $\overset{―}{K},$ we will shade in all the area of $U$ that is *outside* of $K,$ as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071504/assets/74345aeb2a1028e07d155dd357a9bb412860309c99cee37c62380907b3e1bd37.png)

The element in the shaded area is $n.$ This is the only element of $U$ that is not in $K.$ Therefore, the complement of $K$ is

$$
\overset{―}{K}={n}.
$$
